decisive_items: under antipsychotic treatment (risperidone) with antiparkinsonian drug (Biperiden) without treatment withdrawal
response.rationale: Antipsychotic exposure, fever, tachycardia, rigidity, altered consciousness, and elevated CPK strongly indicate neuroleptic malignant syndrome; the reversible splenial lesion is a known associated finding. Catatonia features are present but are part of the NMS syndrome rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Anti-NMDA encephalitis lacks typical seizures, dyskinesias, CSF findings, or teratoma; CPK elevation and antipsychotic exposure favor NMS.
ADEM would typically show multifocal demyelinating lesions, not an isolated reversible splenial lesion without preceding infection or enhancement.
Heat stroke requires environmental exposure; fever and tachycardia are nonspecific and rigidity/CPK elevation with antipsychotic use favor NMS.
Schizophrenia is only the past history; the acute syndrome is a drug-induced complication.
Catatonia features are prominent but fever, autonomic instability, elevated CPK, and antipsychotic use indicate NMS rather than primary catatonia.
Osmotic demyelination is contradicted by explicit absence of hyponatremia or hypoglycemia; the splenial lesion is reversible cytotoxic edema.
Encephalitis is nonspecific and lacks CSF or infectious confirmation; rigidity, CPK elevation, and antipsychotic exposure better support NMS.
